title: Merrick Community in Horton’s Journal, 1742
summary: Azariah Horton’s June 7, 1742 journal entry records a visit to Native people at Merrick during his travels along Long Island’s South Shore.
address_label: Merrick community; meeting place not identified
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as eighteenth-century evidence of Native presence in the Merrick area.
why_this_matters: Horton’s journal records Native people living in Merrick long after colonial land transactions. Their presence is part of a continuing community history that accounts of settlement often overlook.
introduction_content:
In his third missionary journal, Azariah Horton recorded a Merrick visit on June 7, 1742, between his June 6 entry for Rockaway and a June 7 afternoon entry for Fort Neck. He described the Merrick listeners as thankful for the instruction he offered. The account appeared in Christian Monthly History, no. VI (1744), and was later reprinted in Gaynell Stone’s edited The History and Archaeology of the Montauk.

Horton wrote as a Christian missionary. His brief assessment records his own perspective; it does not tell us the listeners’ names or give their independent accounts of the encounter.
history_content:
Horton traveled between Native communities in Rockaway, Merrick, Fort Neck, and Jerusalem near present-day Wantagh. Historian John A. Strong and Zsuzsanna Török trace these journeys in their study of his journals, Taking the Middle Way.

His June 7, 1742 Merrick entry falls between a Rockaway visit the previous day and an afternoon visit to Fort Neck. These journeys offer glimpses of Native community life decades after the earliest colonial land agreements.
whereintheworld_content: Horton visited the Merrick community during his South Shore travels. The location of the 1742 gathering is unknown.
